new_statements.quote: Les phonèmes du kwezo sont au nombre de 21 : 19 segments - 5 voyelles, 2 semi-voyelles et 12 consonnes - et 2 phonèmes de tonalité. Contrairement à ce qui se passe dans d'autres langues bantoues, il n'y a pas d'opposition phonologique de quantité. [§1.9:] On distingue fondamentalement deux phonèmes de tonalité : un haut et un bas. Le tonème haut sera noté par l'accent aigu et le tonème bas par l'accent grave. Seules les voyelles sont tonales. [§1.15.5:] La voyelle de l'avant-dernière syllabe est généralement plus longue que les autres.
new_statements.translation: The phonemes of Kwezo number 21: 19 segments - 5 vowels, 2 semivowels and 12 consonants - and 2 tone phonemes. Unlike what happens in other Bantu languages, there is no phonological opposition of quantity. [§1.9:] Fundamentally two tone phonemes are distinguished: a high and a low. The high toneme will be written with the acute accent and the low toneme with the grave accent. Only vowels bear tone. [§1.15.5:] The vowel of the penultimate syllable is generally longer than the others.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Kwezo is a two-level tone language (H vs L, contour tones arising from H+L sequences on one vowel, with downstep/'abaissement'); vowel length is not contrastive. The description says nothing about word stress or an accent d'intensité; the only prominence-like statement is phonetic: under intonation the vowel of the phrase-penultimate syllable is generally lengthened ([mùmă:vú] 'sous la terre', [ti:ya] 'feu'), and phrase-final high tones may collapse.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal: obligatory vs optional downstep (§1.12-1.13); phrase-final H collapse in free variation with the normal form (§1.15.6); 'generally' hedges the penultimate lengthening (§1.15.5).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level for the tonemes (lexical tone types A/B on nouns, pronouns, infinitives and verb radicals); the penultimate lengthening and H-collapse are stated for the phrase ('phrase', examples are whole utterances), in the Intonation section (§1.15.4-6). Suprasegmental sections 1.9-1.15 (pp. 29-41) were reached only through snippet search, not read in full.
new_statements.identity_note: Forges describes 'kwezo' = Kwese (kikwese), ISO kws, glottocode kwes1244, Guthrie L13 (Forges proposes K53, closest to Mbala K51 and Pende K52), spoken in the Kikwit region between the Kwenge and Lutshima rivers (territoire de Gungu, Kwilu, DRC); 'Pindi' (Lamal 1954) is an alternative name for the same group. No dialect is singled out.
